name: avalonia-designer
description: Create Avalonia projects (C# / VB.NET) and design forms visually with a WYSIWYG drag-and-drop designer and toolbox — with an optional local AI assist that writes handlers and repairs code from a sentence, on your own machine.

commands.title: AI: Add a Model from Hugging Face…
AI: Forget a Model Added from Hugging Face…
AI: Learn the House Rules from My Code…

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.enabled.description: Show the dotted grid overlay on the designer surface (always on top, non-interactive).

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.snapToGrid.description: Snap controls to the grid when moving or resizing them.

enumDescriptions: Use an OpenAI-compatible server on this machine (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp).
Bundle it: the extension builds a small local model server and uses a model it downloads once (no other AI needed).
avaloniaDesigner.assistant.backend.markdownDescription: Where the AI assist gets its model. `bundled` needs nothing installed except the .NET SDK the designer already requires; run **AI: Set Up Local Model…** first. **EXPERIMENTAL FEATURE — USE WITH CAUTION.**

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.ignoreHostChe.markdownDescription: Run the AI assist on a machine the host check refused (not enough memory available for the smallest supported model, or a CPU without AVX2). The check greys the AI section out and explains why; this is the **Use it anyway** escape, for an eGPU, a card that was not detected, or a machine you know can do it. Every start is written to the log.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.modelPath.markdownDescription: The `.gguf` file the bundled runtime loads, set by **AI: Set Up Local Model…**. A downloaded model lives in the extension's global storage.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.threads.description: CPU threads for the local runtime — the extension's own or your own llama-server. 0 picks automatically (one less than the machine has, capped at 8) — more than the physical cores makes generation slower, not faster.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.endpoint.markdownDescription: Base URL of the local server: `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` (LM Studio, the default), `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` (Ollama) or `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (llama.cpp). Leaving it empty falls back to the LM Studio address.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.model.markdownDescription: Model id to ask for. Empty lets the server decide — Ollama has no default, so it needs a name here (e.g. `qwen2.5-coder:7b`).

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.timeoutSecond.description: How long to wait without any output before giving up — the clock restarts with every token, so a slow CPU is fine and a stalled server is caught. Inference in system RAM is slow: 10 s is optimistic for a 3B model, 30 s is normal on an older CPU. A model that thinks before answering is busy, not stalled, so it is not cut off either.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.maxTokens.description: Upper bound on the generated code. 4096 leaves room for a model that thinks before it answers (a reasoning model can spend 800+ tokens on a one-line question); 900 is fine for a coder model that answers directly.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.showDiff.description: Show the model's code as a diff to review before it is applied (the ⚙ Settings panel has the same switch). Turn it off and the code is written straight into the file — still a normal edit, so Ctrl+Z undoes it, and the rule-based checks (a name that already exists, the visibility fix) still run first.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.conventions.markdownDescription: **House rules** for the code the model writes — one short sentence each, e.g. `Indent with 4 spaces.` Every rule is added to each request. *AI: Learn the House Rules from My Code…* measures the patterns your own files already follow and offers the ones that hold almost everywhere; the ⚙ Settings panel edits the list.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.temperature.description: Lower is more literal. Code wants it low: 0.1-0.3.

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.spacingX.description: Horizontal spacing between dots, in design pixels.

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.spacingY.description: Vertical spacing between dots, in design pixels.

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.color.description: Color of the dots (any CSS color, e.g. #9db4d0).

avaloniaDesigner.dotGrid.dotSize.description: Diameter of each dot in pixels.

avaloniaDesigner.crosshair.mode.description: Designer crosshair length: Short = a fixed-length cross; Long = lines reach the edges of the form.

avaloniaDesigner.crosshair.shortLength.description: Total length of the Short crosshair, in pixels.

avaloniaDesigner.crosshair.thickness.description: Thickness of each crosshair line, in pixels.

avaloniaDesigner.crosshair.opacity.description: Opacity of the crosshair, in percent.

avaloniaDesigner.crosshair.color.description: Colour of the crosshair lines. The outline is picked automatically for contrast.

avaloniaDesigner.previewTheme.description: Theme the designer preview renders with: auto = follow the VS Code colour theme (a dark VS Code ≈ a dark OS, so 'System'-themed forms are previewed dark); light/dark force it regardless of an explicit RequestedThemeVariant on the form.

avaloniaDesigner.askEventOnPlace.description: When a control is placed, ask which event to wire (a picker with the control's own events) instead of wiring the default one silently. Interactive controls only (Button, TextBox, CheckBox, ComboBox, ListBox, DataGrid, TabControl, Menu, …); right-click → Add event works for every control either way.

avaloniaDesigner.autoWireDefaultEvent.description: With 'askEventOnPlace' switched off: wire the control's default event silently when it is placed. Set to false to place controls without any event handler (the same choice the picker's Skip button remembers for you).

avaloniaDesigner.codeCheck.mode.description: When the designer re-checks the code-behind against the form (.vb/.cs edited by hand). The check is read-only — it only reports (PROBLEMS pane, canvas badges, Code Fix… list); nothing is ever rewritten. onReturn = every time you come back to the designer tab; onSave = when the code-behind file is saved; onType = while typing (debounced); manual = only when you press Code Fix…

avaloniaDesigner.codeCheck.badges.description: Mark controls on the design surface whose wired event handler is missing with a ⚠ badge (hover it to see which handler). Only shown while the re-check is not 'manual'.

avaloniaDesigner.codeCheck.build.description: When you press Code Fix…, also run the project's own build (dotnet build) and list the compiler's errors and warnings next to the rules' findings — the only way a missing ';' anywhere, a type error or a missing using is ever reported, since the rules are not a compiler. Takes a few seconds (incremental), never runs on the automatic re-checks, and never runs while typing. Switch off if you would rather only see the instant rule-based findings.

avaloniaDesigner.codeCheck.aiRepair.description: When a build error has no rule that can repair it, ask the local model to fix it — but only while the model is already running: nothing here ever starts a model. Each answer is applied, then verified by rebuilding, and an answer that does not bring the project closer to compiling is undone, so your file is left as it was. Requires the AI assist to be enabled.

avaloniaDesigner.publish.packageName.description: Debian package name for the "Publish" button. Empty = the project's assembly name, lowercased (e.g. MyApp becomes myapp). dpkg-deb only accepts lowercase letters, digits, ".", "+" and "-".

avaloniaDesigner.publish.version.description: Version for the published package. Empty = the <Version> in the project file, else 1.0.0. A leading "v" is dropped and "1.0.0-beta" becomes "1.0.0.beta" (a Debian version must start with a digit, and a "-" would split it into upstream/revision).

avaloniaDesigner.publish.maintainer.description: The "Maintainer" field of the published .deb, in the form Name <email>. Debian policy requires it, so it is worth setting once.

avaloniaDesigner.publish.description.description: One-line description shown in the application menu and by apt. Empty = a generic "Standalone application built with Avalonia".

avaloniaDesigner.publish.extraDepends.description: Extra Debian packages the app needs, added to the .deb's "Depends" (e.g. libcanberra0). The .NET runtime and the Avalonia native libraries are declared automatically.

enumDescriptions: CPU build — the default: works everywhere, needs nothing from the GPU.
Vulkan build — puts model layers on the GPU. Downloaded the first time the runtime is built (~130 MB). llama.cpp falls back to the CPU by itself when Vulkan cannot be used.
avaloniaDesigner.assistant.bundledBacken.markdownDescription: Which llama.cpp build the **built-in runtime** runs (the extension's own local model server). Only the GPU-offload field matters after this: the CPU build has no GPU backend, so `max` there offloads nothing — the ⚙ Settings panel says so. This does not affect LM Studio or your own `llama-server`. The command **AI: Built-in Runtime Backend…** sets it too.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.loadContextLe.description: Context length handed to LM Studio when the extension loads a model (0 = recommend one from free RAM). Only used at load time — reload to apply a change.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.loadGpu.description: GPU offload used when the extension loads a model. 'auto' picks 'off' for models over 8 GB, because a shared-memory GPU is slower than the CPU for those.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.loadTtlSecond.description: Unload the model after this many idle seconds (-1 = recommend 15 minutes, 0 = keep it loaded). Only used at load time.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.llamaServerPa.markdownDescription: The `llama-server` binary to run for **My own llama-server** (⤓ Settings → AI, or *AI: Start My llama-server…*). Empty looks in the usual build folders and on `PATH`.

avaloniaDesigner.assistant.llamaServerAr.markdownDescription: Extra command-line flags for that `llama-server`, e.g. `--flash-attn on --no-warmup`. Added **after** the flags the extension computes, so yours win.
